Condition_Defined: extract the health condition, disease, or clinical problem the review investigates, as explicitly stated. Capture the condition name with any qualifiers describing stage, severity, subtype, or anatomical site (e.g., 'type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'major depressive disorder', 'post-stroke upper-limb spasticity'). Do not include disease mechanism, prevalence, or burden (those belong to Condition_Background). Extract each distinct condition as a separate entry.
Population_Defined: extract the group(s) of people the evidence applies to, defined by age, sex, demographic, clinical status, setting, or comorbidities (e.g., 'adults aged 65+ with mild cognitive impairment', 'pregnant women at <20 weeks gestation', 'children under 5 in low-resource settings'). This is the population-level scope of the review, distinct from study-level inclusion criteria (Inclusion_Criteria). Format each as: '[population descriptor]'. Extract each distinct population as a separate entry.
Intervention_Defined: extract the treatment, exposure, intervention, or strategy being studied, including drug name(s) and class, dose, route, device, behavior, or program (e.g., 'metformin 500 mg twice daily, oral', 'cognitive behavioral therapy weekly sessions', 'whole-grain dietary intervention'). Do not capture the comparator (that belongs to Comparator_Defined) or the mechanism of action (that belongs to Intervention_Rationale). Extract each distinct intervention as a separate entry.
Comparator_Defined: extract the control condition, placebo, usual care, alternative treatment, or no-treatment arm against which the intervention is compared (e.g., 'placebo', 'usual care', 'standard pharmacotherapy', 'sham acupuncture', 'no intervention'). Do not extract the intervention itself (that belongs to Intervention_Defined). Extract each distinct comparator as a separate entry.
Timing_Intervention: extract the timing, duration, frequency, or treatment period of the intervention itself (e.g., 'daily for 12 weeks', 'single dose at week 0', 'continuous use for >=6 months'). This is the timing of the intervention, distinct from when outcomes were measured (Outcome_Timeframe). Extract each timing descriptor as a separate entry.
Purpose_Aim: extract the explicit aim, objective, or research question of the review (what the review sought to determine), paraphrased or quoted from the review (e.g., 'To assess the effects of statins on cardiovascular mortality in adults', 'To evaluate the safety and efficacy of GLP-1 agonists for weight loss in obese adults without diabetes'). Extract each distinct stated aim as a separate entry.
Primary_Benefit_Outcome: extract the primary benefit (efficacy) outcome the review evaluates - the main efficacy endpoint pre-specified by the authors. Include only outcomes the review explicitly labels as primary, main, or central. Do not include secondary efficacy outcomes (Secondary_Benefit_Outcome) or safety/adverse-effect outcomes (Harm_Safety_Outcome). Format each as: '[outcome name]: [brief definition or measurement scale, if given]'. Extract each primary outcome as a separate entry.
Secondary_Benefit_Outcome: extract additional benefit (efficacy) outcomes that are not labeled primary - outcomes the review tracks alongside the primary endpoint to give a fuller picture of efficacy. Do not include adverse-effect outcomes (Harm_Safety_Outcome) or the primary outcome (Primary_Benefit_Outcome). Extract each secondary benefit outcome as a separate entry.
Harm_Safety_Outcome: extract unwanted effects, adverse events, harms, side effects, or safety outcomes assessed by the review (e.g., 'serious adverse events', 'gastrointestinal bleeding', 'all-cause mortality'). Include both common and serious harms when both are reported. Do not include benefit outcomes (Primary_Benefit_Outcome or Secondary_Benefit_Outcome). Extract each harm or safety outcome as a separate entry.
Outcome_Timeframe: extract when (after intervention start) outcomes were assessed (e.g., 'at 12 weeks', 'at 1 year', 'at end of treatment', 'at 30 days post-discharge'). This is distinct from the duration of the intervention itself (Timing_Intervention). Format each as: '[outcome]: [timeframe]'. Extract each timeframe as a separate entry.
Outcome_Definition: extract how an outcome is explained or operationalized in plain language - definitions or descriptions that clarify what the outcome means or how it is measured (e.g., 'serious adverse event: any event requiring hospitalization', 'remission: PHQ-9 score below 5'). Format each as: '[outcome name]: [plain-language definition]'. Extract each definition as a separate entry.
Benefit_Direction: extract the stated direction of effect for benefit outcomes (e.g., 'increase', 'decrease', 'no difference', 'improvement', 'reduction', 'little to no difference'). Do not include effects on harms (Harm_Direction). Format each as: '[outcome]: [direction]'. Extract each directional finding as a separate entry.
Harm_Direction: extract the stated direction of effect for harm/safety outcomes (e.g., 'increase in adverse events', 'no difference in serious harms', 'reduction in gastrointestinal side effects'). Format each as: '[harm outcome]: [direction]'. Extract each directional finding as a separate entry.
Magnitude_Descriptor: extract qualitative magnitude qualifiers used to describe effect size in plain language (e.g., 'slightly', 'little to no', 'small', 'moderate', 'large', 'substantial'). These are the verbal hedges authors use alongside numerical results; do not include the numerical effect itself (Quantitative_Data). Format each as: '[outcome]: [magnitude descriptor]'. Extract each magnitude descriptor as a separate entry.
Quantitative_Data: extract numerical results reported in the review - risk ratios, odds ratios, hazard ratios, mean differences, percentages, absolute risk differences, NNT, confidence intervals, p-values, etc. (e.g., 'RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.94', '15% vs 22% (absolute reduction 7%)', 'mean difference -2.3 points (95% CI -3.5 to -1.1)'). Link each figure to its outcome and comparison when available. Extract each numerical result as a separate entry.
Evidence_Absence: extract explicit statements that no data, no studies, or insufficient evidence was found for an outcome or comparison (e.g., 'No studies reported on long-term mortality', 'We found no eligible trials for this comparison'). Do not infer absence; require explicit statements. This is narrower than Evidence_Gaps (which covers broader limitations). Format each as: '[outcome/topic]: no data found' or quote the relevant phrasing. Extract each absence statement as a separate entry.
Certainty_Level: extract the confidence/certainty rating expressed by the review for a given finding (e.g., 'very low certainty', 'low certainty', 'moderate certainty', 'high certainty', 'very uncertain', 'GRADE: moderate'). Format each as: '[outcome]: [certainty level]'. Extract each certainty rating as a separate entry.
Reason_Downgrading: extract the reasons given for a lower certainty rating, such as study limitations, risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, publication bias, or small sample size (e.g., 'downgraded for risk of bias and imprecision'). Format each as: '[outcome]: [reason(s) for downgrading]'. Extract each downgrading reason as a separate entry.
Study_Design: extract the study design(s) of the studies included in the review (e.g., 'RCTs', 'cluster-randomized trials', 'observational cohort studies', 'cross-over trials'). This refers to the designs of the included primary studies, not the review's own design. Extract each distinct study design as a separate entry.
Number_Studies: extract the total number of studies included in the review (e.g., '12 studies', '34 RCTs included'). If multiple counts exist (e.g., per comparison or subgroup), format each as: '[count]: [scope/comparison]'. Extract each count as a separate entry.
Total_Sample_Size: extract the total number of participants across all included studies (e.g., 'N = 4,532 participants', '2,108 patients across 12 trials'). If reported per comparison or per arm, extract each with context as a separate entry.
Search_Strategy: extract how the literature search was conducted - databases searched, search dates, inclusion of grey literature, language restrictions (e.g., 'MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL searched through January 2025', 'no language restrictions', 'included unpublished trial registry entries'). Extract each distinct element as a separate entry, or as one comprehensive entry if the review describes it succinctly.
Inclusion_Criteria: extract the eligibility criteria the review used to include or exclude studies (e.g., 'RCTs only', 'adults >=18 years', 'studies with >=12 weeks follow-up', 'published in English'). These are criteria for studies, not for participants within studies (Population_Defined). Extract each criterion as a separate entry.
Evidence_Gaps: extract missing outcomes, populations, comparisons, or settings the review notes as having insufficient data (e.g., 'No studies in children', 'Limited data on long-term safety', 'No head-to-head trials versus newer agents'). This is broader than explicit no-data statements (Evidence_Absence). Extract each gap as a separate entry.
Condition_Background: extract disease mechanism, prevalence, progression, natural history, burden, or pathophysiology described as context (e.g., 'Alzheimer's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder affecting approximately 50 million people worldwide'). This is context about the condition itself, distinct from the condition the review studies (Condition_Defined). Extract each background statement as a separate entry.
Intervention_Rationale: extract the biological, behavioral, or theoretical reason the intervention is expected to work - its mechanism of action or hypothesized pathway (e.g., 'SSRIs increase synaptic serotonin levels, hypothesized to alleviate depressive symptoms'). This is distinct from what the intervention is (Intervention_Defined). Extract each rationale as a separate entry.
Definition_Technical_Terms: extract plain-language explanations of medical, statistical, or methodological terminology used in the review (e.g., 'odds ratio: a measure comparing the odds of an outcome between two groups', 'placebo: an inactive treatment used for comparison'). Format each as: '[term]: [plain-language definition]'. Extract each defined term as a separate entry.
Applicability: extract statements about whom the findings apply to, where they generalize, or explicit limits on generalizability (e.g., 'Findings apply primarily to adults aged 18-65 in high-income settings; generalizability to children or low-resource settings is unclear'). Extract each applicability statement as a separate entry.
Evidence_Currency: extract how up-to-date the review is - search date, publication date, or any explicit currency statement (e.g., 'Search current to March 2024', 'Last updated in 2023'). Extract each currency-related statement as a separate entry.
